title: spec: add a type-independent document self-check step (RFC P1)
description:
SOURCE RFC: rfcs/inbox/rfc-self-spec-document-self-check.md — proposal P1
Severity: blocker | Origin: self | runs_observed: 1 | model: claude-opus-5

STATUS: triage stopped at step 4 by explicit human instruction. Nothing
was implemented. The classification below is a RECOMMENDATION, not an
approval.
RECOMMENDED CLASSIFICATION: adopt-now, with the refinement below.

PROBLEM
The `spec` skill's authoring workflow has exactly one verification step
and it is scoped to a single document type. plugin/skills/spec/SKILL.md:210
reads: "**Preflight feature blueprints.** Before setting a feature
blueprint to `ready-for-review`, run the decision sweep and self-check
against `references/blueprint-readiness-checklist.md`". Steps 1-5 and 7
contain no verification instruction at all, so ADRs, FRDs, standards
documents, contracts and the architecture blueprints are authored with no
check. Step 3 mandates EARS and nothing ever asks whether the finished
document complies. Consequence recorded by the RFC: a standards document
reached `ready-for-review` carrying three compound SHALL requirements,
which plugin/skills/spec/references/ears-guide.md:125 forbids — "**One
requirement per sentence.** Never join two SHALLs with \"and.\"" They were
caught only because the agent invented an ad-hoc parser; nothing in the
skill asked for that check.

CONCRETE CHANGE
(a) Insert a new step in the authoring workflow, before step 7's retro
offer, with this text:

  **N. Self-check the finished document.** Before setting any document
  to `ready-for-review`, run `references/document-readiness-checklist.md`
  against it. Fix what it reports and re-run; do not set
  `ready-for-review` while any check fails. (Feature blueprints
  additionally run the blueprint readiness checklist in step 6 — that
  one is about groomability, this one about conformance.)

(b) Create plugin/skills/spec/references/document-readiness-checklist.md
holding these eight type-independent checks:

  1. Frontmatter parses as YAML and declares title, description, slug,
     type, status, updated_at.
  2. The slug matches the registry's rule for this type.
  3. status is a value from the controlled vocabulary.
  4. Every normative statement uses an EARS pattern.
  5. No requirement joins two modal verbs with "and".
  6. No prose line exceeds 80 characters (tables, URLs, fences exempt).
  7. Every template instruction comment block has been deleted.
  8. Every [[slug]] reference resolves to an existing document.

REFINEMENT REQUIRED (from triage — apply this, do not copy the RFC text
verbatim)
Checks 1, 2, 3, 6 and 8 restate rules already normative elsewhere:
template-authoring-standards.md v0.12 (Metadata/Frontmatter sec. 54,
Slug Conventions sec. 62-118, Line Length sec. 42, Reference Validation
sec. 433) and cross-document-references.md. The framework forbids
duplication, and blueprint-readiness-checklist.md states the pattern
explicitly: "The checks are defined only here — the skills reference
this document rather than restating it, so authoring and grooming can
never disagree about what 'groomable' means." So the new checklist MUST
cite those standards for the checks they already own, and state in its
own voice only what is genuinely new: check 4 (EARS coverage), check 5
(compound modal verbs), check 7 (instruction blocks deleted).

FILES TOUCHED
- plugin/skills/spec/SKILL.md — insert the step; bump frontmatter
  version "1.3" -> "1.4" (MINOR)
- plugin/skills/spec/references/document-readiness-checklist.md — new
  file; needs frontmatter per template-authoring-standards (title,
  description, slug, type: standards, status, updated_at, version)
- plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json — version 0.7.0 -> 0.8.0 (MINOR)

ACCEPTANCE
- The new step appears in the authoring workflow before the retro offer
  and applies to every document type.
- document-readiness-checklist.md exists, is under 100 lines or carries
  a Contents section, and cites rather than restates checks 1/2/3/6/8.
- All touched files hold 80-column lines.
- Both version bumps applied.
- scripts/check-skills.sh exits 0.

CONSTRAINT: do not weaken or widen references/blueprint-readiness-checklist.md
— it gates groomability and is a separate concern (the RFC's own Non-Goal).

title: standards-template: slug is independent of filename (RFC P3)
description:
SOURCE RFC: rfcs/inbox/rfc-self-spec-document-self-check.md — proposal P3
Severity: snag | Origin: self | runs_observed: 1 | model: claude-opus-5

STATUS: triage stopped at step 4 by explicit human instruction. Nothing
was implemented. Classification below is a RECOMMENDATION, not approval.
RECOMMENDED CLASSIFICATION: adopt-now, with the citation correction below.

PROBLEM
The standards template raises a slug constraint and says nothing about
how it relates to the filename. plugin/skills/spec/references/
standards-template.md:29-32 reads: "This type has no fixed prefix (it is
the registry's one exception). Use a descriptive slug ending in an
approved role noun: -standards, -policy, -guidelines, or -constraints
(e.g. security-standards, data-retention-policy)." The RFC's run had a
requested filename (skill-best-practices.md) ending in none of those
nouns, and had to leave the bundle the References table prescribes
(SKILL.md:244 sends standards work to standards-template.md +
ears-guide.md only) to discover that slug and filename are independent.

CONCRETE CHANGE
Append to the Slug instruction block at standards-template.md:29-32:

  The slug is independent of the filename. A reference resolves against
  this document's frontmatter `slug`, never its path, so a file may be
  named for how humans will look for it while the slug carries the
  registry-conforming identifier.

CITATION CORRECTION (found during triage — the RFC misattributes)
The RFC attributes the sentence "A reference resolves against the target
document's frontmatter `slug` — never a file path" to
template-authoring-standards.md. That text is verbatim correct but lives
in plugin/skills/spec/references/cross-document-references.md:44-45.
Verified during triage by grep. If the implementing edit cites a source,
it MUST cite cross-document-references.md (or [[cross-document-references]]),
NOT template-authoring-standards.md.

FILES TOUCHED
- plugin/skills/spec/references/standards-template.md — append to the
  Slug block; bump the instruction-block "Version: 1.1" -> "Version: 1.2"
  (MINOR)
- plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json — 0.7.0 -> 0.8.0 (MINOR; shared with
  the other RFC beads — if several land, bump once)

ACCEPTANCE
- The sentence is inside the template's HTML instruction comment block
  (so it is deleted with the block by an author), not in the document body.
- Instruction-block Version bumped.
- 80-column lines held.
- scripts/check-skills.sh exits 0.

DO NOT: add template-authoring-standards.md to the standards row's
bundle in SKILL.md:244. The RFC considered and rejected that as the more
expensive of two fixes (it enlarges a deliberately small bundle).

title: spec: state where a new document is written (RFC P2)
description:
SOURCE RFC: rfcs/inbox/rfc-self-spec-document-self-check.md — proposal P2
Severity: snag | Origin: self | runs_observed: 1 | model: claude-opus-5

STATUS: triage stopped at step 4 by explicit human instruction. Nothing
was implemented. Classification below is a RECOMMENDATION, not approval.
RECOMMENDED CLASSIFICATION: adopt-now (as proposed).

PROBLEM
The `spec` authoring workflow never says where a new document is
written. plugin/skills/spec/SKILL.md:188 reads "1. **Pick the template**
from `references/` (table below) and copy it as the starting point for
the new document", and SKILL.md:190 ("2. **Follow the embedded
instructions.**") covers the comment blocks. Neither names a destination
path. The standards template specifies the slug rule
(standards-template.md:29) but not the location. Verified during triage:
no step in the workflow states a destination. Absent a human-supplied
path the agent guesses, so document location is decided by whoever
happens to have an opinion.

CONCRETE CHANGE
Replace step 1 at plugin/skills/spec/SKILL.md:188-189 with:

  1. **Pick the template** from `references/` (table below) and copy it
     as the starting point for the new document. **Write it under the
     project's spec root** — `docs/` unless the project's `AGENTS.md` or
     `CLAUDE.md` names another — in a subdirectory for its type
     (`docs/adrs/`, `docs/standards/`, `docs/blueprints/`, …). WHEN the
     project has an established location for that type, follow it; the
     frontmatter index does not depend on location, but humans do.

FILES TOUCHED
- plugin/skills/spec/SKILL.md — edit step 1; bump frontmatter version
  "1.3" -> "1.4" (MINOR; shared with the P1 bead agent-plugins-fiu —
  if both land, bump once)
- plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json — 0.7.0 -> 0.8.0 (MINOR; shared)

ACCEPTANCE
- Step 1 names a destination and preserves the AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md
  escape hatch (it must not hardcode a layout onto projects that already
  have one).
- Lines stay within 80 columns.
- scripts/check-skills.sh exits 0.

title: templates: placeholder section lists convey nothing (RFC P4)
description:
SOURCE RFC: rfcs/inbox/rfc-self-spec-document-self-check.md — proposal P4
Severity: polish | Origin: self | runs_observed: 1 | model: claude-opus-5

STATUS: triage stopped at step 4 by explicit human instruction. Nothing
was implemented. Classification below is a RECOMMENDATION, not approval.
RECOMMENDED CLASSIFICATION: DEFER — and the change as written is
DEFECTIVE. Do not implement it as proposed; see the blocking defect.

READ THIS FIRST: this bead is NOT ready to execute as an edit. It is
ready as a decision. If dispatched, the correct outcome is either
(a) leave it deferred, or (b) reshape the change per "IF LATER ADOPTED"
below. Applying the RFC's literal text will break the repo's own gate.

PROBLEM
plugin/skills/spec/references/standards-template.md:15-18 reads:

  Sections (complete each, then delete its instruction block)
    - <Major Category>
    - <Another Major Category>
    - References

For a template whose sections are author-defined, this enumerates
placeholders and conveys little. It contrasts with the fixed-section
templates (ADR: Context / Decision / Alternatives Considered /
Consequences / References) where the same list is a genuine map.

BLOCKING DEFECT IN THE CHANGE AS WRITTEN (found during triage)
scripts/check-skills.sh:132-136 gates every reference file over 100
lines:

  for p in glob.glob('plugin/skills/*/references/*.md'):
      if '/shared/' in p: continue
      t = open(p).read()
      if len(t.split('\n')) > 100 and not re.search(r'^#+ Contents|^Sections \(complete', t, re.M):
          err(p, "over 100 lines with no table of contents")

standards-template.md is 218 lines. The RFC's replacement text
("Structure: one `##` per major requirement category, `###` per
subcategory, then a References section. ...") matches neither
`^#+ Contents` nor `^Sections \(complete`, so adopting P4 verbatim makes
scripts/check-skills.sh fail on the very file it edits.

WHY DEFER RATHER THAN ADOPT OR REJECT
- No run cost. The RFC's own justification is "worth doing while the
  section lists are being reviewed for other reasons" — i.e. no
  independent evidence that the placeholder list harmed a run.
- Wider than one file. Ten templates carry the same "Sections (complete
  each" construct: adr, component-blueprint, container-blueprint,
  contract, feature-blueprint, frd, module-blueprint, standards,
  system-blueprint, work-order. The real change is taxonomy-wide, not a
  one-file edit, and the RFC only proposes the author-defined-section
  case.
- Hold for a second, independent project reporting the same friction.

IF LATER ADOPTED, the reshaped change must
- keep the "Sections (complete" marker OR introduce a `## Contents`
  heading in every file it touches, OR deliberately amend
  scripts/check-skills.sh:135 to accept the new form; and
- state which of the ten templates are in scope and which keep their
  enumerated list; and
- bump each touched template's instruction-block Version, plus
  plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json.

ACCEPTANCE (for the deferral as it stands)
- No files edited.
- Bead remains open with labels rfc-triage + theme:template-ergonomics
  so recurrence across projects can be counted.
